swaps.why: Six miles around the water with downtown on one side and houseboats on the other. If what you actually miss is the crowd, Green Lake is the one — 2.8 flat miles and never empty.

swaps.from: Boston Common and the Public Garden
swaps.why: A conservatory, a climbable water tower, an art museum, and enough grass to lie on. Capitol Hill treats it as a front garden.
Low brick, independent shops, and a farmers market down the middle of it every Sunday of the year.
Bigger, wilder, and it ends at a lighthouse on a bluff over the Sound. Green Lake is the social one; this is the one you go to be alone.

swaps.to: Olympic Sculpture Park into the Elliott Bay Trail
swaps.why: Art on a slope down to the water, then flat waterfront miles north past the container cranes.
The same sit-on-a-slope-and-watch-everyone energy, with meaningfully less sun and a reflecting pool.
230 acres of trees with soft paths through them, running down to the water at Foster Island.
27 paved miles, though it threads through neighbourhoods rather than running along a single shore. Ballard to Bothell without touching a road.
Much smaller, much closer to town, and it is Rainier behind the skyline instead of a sign on a hill.
